utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning, technical booth, the interpreters, everyone present in the courtroom; good morning to counsel for the Prosecution and for the Defence. We will resume our work, and I see that Mr. Nikolic is ready to begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, and thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I begin by asking the usher for his assistance. I have three documents which I should like to tender into evidence. This morning, those documents were marked for identification by the Registry. I also have copies for members of the Trial Chamber. Your Honours, I have just provided the Registry with all three original documents and translations into French and English, and I hope Your Honours have copies now too. These three documents were previously, through a Defence brief of the 12th of February this year, produced to the Tribunal as an attachment to the brief for their inclusion in the evidence, pursuant to Rule 89(C) of the Rules of Procedure. May I begin my opening statement by referring to these documents. The first document, marked as Defence Exhibit D3/2, is the original of a certificate on the completion of the secondary school for catering. This document confirms the date when Mr. Milojica Kos graduated from this catering educational institution and became a waiter in 1981. The second exhibit has been marked D4/2. It is the original certificate issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska, that is, the Omarska Police Station, which certifies that Milojica Kos became a member of the reserve police force on the 6th of May, 1992, and that he remained in this police station department as a reserve policeman until the 8th of November, 1992. The third document is Exhibit D5/2. It is the original certificate issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska and the Secondary School for Internal Affairs in Banja Luka certifying that Milojica Kos completed a course and became a policeman. The certificate is dated November 12th, 1993. Your Honours, at the beginning of this case in his opening statement, the Prosecutor said, and I shall paraphrase if I may, that this is a trial of the government policy of persecution and ethnic cleansing and stated that the accused would endeavour to persuade the Trial Chamber that they had not planned, advocated, or instigated and ordered a campaign of persecution and terror, but that that policy came from the top of the government leadership which, as the Prosecutor himself said on the occasion, may even be true. The main issue before us is whether the citizens of ex-Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina wanted and desired this cruel war and bloodshed throughout their areas. They were not consulted about that, nor did they decide about it. They were drawn into the furor of conflict, ordinary people, workers, craftsmen, tradesmen, and as we see, waiters included. They were mobilised in 1992, and this mobilisation went on round the clock, after which they were deployed into various military and police formations whereby they had very little choice. Instead of the tools of their trade, being drafted, they were issued weapons, and they took up their positions that were assigned to them, as would the majority of citizens and subjects of any country in the world swept by war. One such individual was Mr. Milojica Kos who was a waiter and an employee in a catering establishment and was, like many other inhabitants of his village, mobilised during those wartime years. Your Honours, for Your Honours to be able to get a full picture of one of the defendants in this courtroom, the Defence of Mr. Milojica Kos will do its best during its case to demonstrate who Mr. Milojica Kos is. You will, Your Honours, hear a little about the background of Mr. Milojica Kos, what kind of setting he grew up in and in what kind of family. Through witness testimony as well as the documents that will be produced, the Defence will seek to explain that Mr. Milojica Kos is an ordinary and simple man who graduated from secondary catering school at the beginning of the 1980s. Until war broke out in ex-Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, Milojica Kos did his job as a waiter serving guests in restaurants and cafes that he was employed in for more than ten the years. Your Honours, you will hear that when war began in the region of Prijedor in April 1992, like the majority of other able-bodied men of age, Mr. Milojica Kos was drafted to the reserve police force at the police station department in Omarska. At the beginning of May 1992, when he became a reserve policeman, Mr. Milojica Kos had no experience whatsoever in the work of the reserve police force. Defence witnesses or, to be more precise, some of them, by conveying their personal experiences that they lived through themselves and similar situations that they were found in, will explain to you, Your Honours, what young reserve officers did at the beginning of the war in 1992 as members of certain police formations, and they will also explain when the reserve police force was mobilised. The witnesses will also tell Your Honours what they know, what they experienced, and through those testimonies, the destiny will be able to be identified of hundreds of thousands of young citizens throughout the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina when the war broke out; war, a word which, for those young generations, was a word without meaning in those days, what that word really meant for the destiny of men. Your Honours, during the Defence case of Mr. Milojica Kos, you will hear when Milojica Kos acquired his initial knowledge about police work, discipline, the Rules of Service, and thereby also how and when Mr. Milojica Kos transferred from the reserve force to active-duty service and became a junior policeman with very basic knowledge of the job assigned to him as a policeman. You will also hear that he had elementary knowledge as to his rights and duties and thereby be in a position to gain a realistic understanding of the situation of Mr. Milojica Kos in the period of June and July 1992. Your Honours, by presenting evidence - oral testimony and written documents - the Defence will seek, through evidence tendered, to round off the picture about Mr. Milojica Kos and try to show whether a person with such a personality could have been, as I mentioned at the beginning of this opening statement and as alleged in the opening statement by the Prosecution, a man who had planned, advocated, ordered, instigated, aided and abetted the ethnic campaign of persecution and terror as part of the government's policy of persecution and ethnic cleansing in the relevant area in the summer of 1992. That ends my opening statement, Your Honours. Before I call our first witness, I should like to notify Your Honours that Mr. O'Sullivan and myself, being gentlemen, would like to give our lady co-counsel, Ms. Nikolic, the chance to examine first. It has been ruled by the Trial Chamber that Ms. Nikolic may be allowed to examine the witness, and this document has been filed with the registry. Your Honours, may we call our first witness to the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Nikolic, before beginning, I think we can deal with a question of your documents. I don't think there is any objection on the part of the Prosecution to the admission of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see they're confirming that, no objection. In that case, the documents have been admitted. And yes, we discussed this matter once, that is, the possibility of Ms. Nikolic taking part in our work, and we have consulted the registry about it. If there is approval by the accused, then the Chamber also agrees. I have already consulted with my colleagues, but I think that Ms. Nikolic has been designated legal assistant of your team, so it is up to the registry to take that into account. Her status in terms of remuneration does not change as a result of this. Therefore, do you have any comment to make, Mr. Nikolic? I see you nodding your head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like Ms. Nikolic to be able to begin with the examination-in-chief of the first witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you have heard the conditions. We have to take that into account because Ms. Nikolic is legal assistant and not co-counsel, and there is the problem of remuneration. But I'll give the floor Madam Registrar. Has the situation been regulated from the standpoint of the registry?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the standpoint of the registry, I don't think the position has been officially regulated. It has to be done as quickly as possible, but it is always up to the Chamber to grant this possibility on condition that the accused agrees for the legal assistant to examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we already have two counsel in the Defence counsel team, that is why I asked the registry. And as we heard, the condition is that her status in terms of remuneration will not change so that Ms. Nikolic may examine the witness. She is not acting as co-counsel but only as legal assistant. That is simply to let you know that. If the accused agrees and the registry, who have given me this note, and the agreement of the Chamber, then you can continue working in the status that you have in this Tribunal, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence calls the first witness, Mrs. Nada Curcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Nada Curcic. Can you hear me? Very well, thank you. Will you now please read the solemn declaration that the usher is giving to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please come a little closer to the microphone. This is good. Now, first of all you will be answering questions that will be put to you by Ms. Nikolic whom you already know. She's standing on your left-hand side. You may proceed, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Thank you for issuing your authorisation for me to conduct the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Curcic.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Ms. Curcic, you know who I am and in what capacity I am here. Before we proceed with your testimony about the facts of the case, would you please state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Nada Curcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is your maiden name?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Kos.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 25th of September, 1966.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you complete your elementary education?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: In Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you continue with your education after that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you complete your secondary education?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is your profession? What is your occupation today?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I am a seamstress.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you have a family of your own?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Chamber where you live today.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: In the village of Sivnica, in the Blace municipality, in Serbia, that is, in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't understand her profession. Can she repeat that? Seamstress?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind, Ms. Curcic, and tell us once again what your occupation is?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I'm a seamstress.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Okay, we understand it now. Thank you. Do you know a gentleman by the name of Milojica Kos?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He's my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where was Milojica Kos born, and when?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He was born on the 1st of April, 1963, in Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you and Milojica grow up together?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the family house of your parents?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where is that house located?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: In the village of Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you tell this Honourable Chamber something about the village of Lamovita, where you grew up?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: It is a very small village which is situated near Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How far, approximately, is it from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: About 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other brothers or sisters?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have one more brother whose name is Miodrag.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does he have a family of his own?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes. He is no longer living with his parents. He has a family of his own.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are either of your parents alive?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Our father is alive; our mother died in a traffic accident.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Ms. Curcic, how old were you at the time when this accident happened?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I was four years old, going on five.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How old was your brother Kos at that time?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He was seven years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you get married?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you leave your parents' house after you got married?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you move to?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I moved to Sivnica, that is, to Yugoslavia, to Serbia, to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. municipality of Blace.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In order for Their Honours to understand, can you tell us how far that is from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: About 700 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After 1984, when you left your family house, were you in contact with your family and with your brother?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: We would, first of all, call each other on the telephone. We wrote to each other. I would visit them there; they would come to pay me a visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How often did you visit your family?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: One to two times a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where Milojica Kos went to elementary school?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: In Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After he completed his elementary education, did he continue to go to school?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did, in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know which school he went to in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Milojica went to the secondary school for catering.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when he completed that secondary school, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I think that he completed it in 1981.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What did he become then?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He became a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After your education, both his and yours, after your childhood and growing up together, did you socialise with young men and women of other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes. We never paid much attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your family, at home, what was the attitude of your father, and then later on of your stepmother, to members of other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: We never discussed this issue of ethnic background at home. Everybody was welcome in our house. We socialised with everybody; everybody came to our house regardless of what ethnic community they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me now briefly discuss one particular matter in relation to your brother. Did he, at one point in time, start to build his own house in Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where in Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: On the same lot where our family houses are located.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That lot, did it belong to your family?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What about your other brother? Where is his house?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: His house is also on the same lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did your brother start building his own house?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he finish it?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He just put the roof on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean when you say that he only put the roof on the house?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Well, the house only has a roof in addition, of course, to the outside walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can one live in that house at this point?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you last see that house of your brother, Milojica?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Not long ago. In January.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: This year, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So you went to Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the Slava celebration with my father.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like the assistance of the usher at this point, please. Would you please put this photograph on the ELMO. But before that, could the photograph be marked for identification? According to our records, it should be Exhibit D6/2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. The document is marked for identification, D6/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please place the photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Ms. Curcic, would you please have a look at this photograph and tell us what it shows?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: This is our family house, the one in which we grew up.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And who is living in this house today?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: My father and my stepmother.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photograph can be removed from the ELMO, Mr. Usher, thank you. And could you give us the second document, please. After this, I should like to ask the usher to give us the second photograph which should be marked as D7/2, and to place the photograph on the ELMO so that the witness can tell us what it shows.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Ms. Curcic, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That is, do you know what it shows?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. This is Milojica's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Is that the house that you just described for us?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When was it brought to the present condition?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was anything done with the house afterwards?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does it still look the same?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The photograph can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We have seen all these photographs. You have told us about your family, your property. If you can just tell us one more piece of information: What is the distance between Milojica's house, your family house, and your brother's house, your other brother's house? How big is that property?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Milojica's house is maybe 20 metres away from my family house where my father and stepmother live, and my brother's house is on the same lot, perhaps some 30 metres away from Milojica's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Until 1992, did Milojica have any other occupation except that of a waiter?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Not that I knew of. That was all he did all that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you live in 1991?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I lived in Sivnica in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You told the Judges how far that is. Now, if you can please tell us how big that town is?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: It's actually a very small village, not far from the town of Blace, and Blace has about 5.000 inhabitants, including all surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did Milojica come to visit you in that village in 1991?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would he stay there for a while?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What did you and Milojica do when he would come to visit you in Blace?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He tried to work there. He worked for about two months, and he worked as a waiter there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: In Blace.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he work in a catering establishment there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he worked in a small cafe.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Who worked there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: We both did. He worked there as a waiter, and I worked in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long did you work together there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: For two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Why did you stop working there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Because the owner of the cafe increased the rent twice, so he had no interest in continuing working there any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After that, did Milojica stay with you in Blace?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He stayed on for a little while, and afterwards he left for Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was that Milojica left Blace, if you can give us the month approximately?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: It was in fall or winter 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what he did after he returned to Lamovita in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't think that he had any job at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were raised together, that you grew up together, you probably know your brother very well. Can you tell us what kind of a young man Milojica Kos was?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He was an exceptional brother. He was a very good friend. He was a quiet and composed young man. I can only say all the best about him. He was always welcome in every group of people within the family, in our neighbourhood. People were happy to see him around.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he have many friends?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he have any interests, any pursuits in his free time?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He was involved in all kinds of sports, jogging, for example. That was what he did in his spare time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he practice any sport in particular?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Football and basketball mostly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was the relationship between your brother Milojica and his parents, his father and his stepmother? Did he help them, for example, later in life?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He always took care of them. He was very mindful of their needs. If they felt sick he was always there, around. He took very good care of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was it easy for Milojica to make friends with new people?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude that people had towards him while you were growing up together and later on when you would visit each other for family celebrations?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Everybody had a very good opinion about him. Everybody liked him. I don't know of any problems that he would have had with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was Milojica interested in politics and political events?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No, never. He never discussed politics. He was never interested in them, he would never let us discuss it during our get-togethers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He was simply not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he go out at night to cafes, restaurants?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he ever have a fight? Did he ever quarrel with people when he went out?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard of any such thing involving him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And one final question: Could you briefly describe for the Judges the temperament and the character of your brother?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: My brother is a very quiet, level-headed man, always willing to help others, a person who never had any problems whatsoever with other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. This concludes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Nikolic. Mr. Waidyaratne. Ms. Curcic, you will now be answering questions that will be put to you by the counsel for the Prosecution, Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Waidyaratne, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Curcic. Ms. Curcic, you spoke in detail about your brother, and you said that he was a good brother, a good friend, and a fine man. What about your other brother, Miodrag, where is he?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He is in Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he help the family too, or was it only Milojica who helped the family?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not as much as Milojica, because he got married very young and had a family of his own, he had children, so he didn't have as much opportunity to help his family as Milojica did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So Milojica was very close to your family, especially the father and the stepmother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, you spoke about Milojica, about his education. Do you remember whether he served in the military, whether he did his compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, like everybody else, like all our young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During that time, do you know that he was based in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you remember during which year that was?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: After he completed his secondary education, in 1982, 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he discuss what he did during the time that he served in the military?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I think that he was a cook there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he say that he had training in the use of weapons, that he underwent training? Did he say that he served in the infantry?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't think -- no, he didn't discuss it in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So you don't know as to whether he was a cook or whether he served in the infantry, which gave him training in the use of weapons and other equipment?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I know that he once told me or wrote to me that he was working in a kitchen as a cook.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, about your family, about your stepmother, how was she? When did she come into the family?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I was very small at the time, very young, when she came, and as far as I can remember and according to what other people told me, I think that it was a year or two years after the death of our mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So you had known your stepmother for quite a long time, from your small days.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What is the physical condition of her? Did she suffer from any illness?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did Milojica say, during the time of 1990, 1991, whether she had to see a doctor, whether she was suffering from any illness?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes. She had an open fracture of her leg at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did Milojica say that he took good care of her, that he took her to see the doctors in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, she was in hospital there and I visited her there myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know the doctor who treated her, your stepmother?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No, I did not, because I had come from Serbia for two or three days just to see her, to see how she was. But he was the one who took care of her, about the doctor and everything else that needed to be done or obtained. After that, after my visit, I went back to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did Milojica mention the name of Dr. Begic to you during that time as a person who treated your stepmother?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No, no. We spoke about her condition, about how she felt at the moment, what other things needed to be done, but we didn't talk about the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When you were in the hospital, when you went to the hospital, did you meet any doctors there? Did any doctor by the name of Dr. Begic meet you?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No. I was visiting only during those hours when visits were allowed, and usually doctors do not walk around the hospital during those hours. I talked to my stepmother, to my brother, to whoever happened to be visiting at the time, but I didn't talk to any of the doctors.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, I will come to the year of 1992. Did you know as to where Milojica worked in 1992, in the month of April?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No. In 1992, in January of this year, I was at my parents, at the Slava, the patron saint's day celebration. He was at home and he was not working at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Just referring to the month of January 1992, did you know what he was doing, what Milojica was doing in 1992, May, in the month of May?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him after you saw him in January 1992, during the period of May, June, July, and August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After you met him in January 1992, when was the last time that you met him after that, after you met him in January 1992?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I saw him in January 1992 for the last time in 1992, and then we maintained contact on the telephone. After that, I did not see him in 1992 because the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So when did you see him -- other than the telephone contact you had in the year 1992, when did you see him then, after that, after January 1992?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I saw him in 1993, again in January, again for the patron saint's day celebration, when I went for a family visit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That was in Omarska, in Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Curcic, you said that you spoke to him over the phone, you had telephone contact. Did you ask him as to what he was doing in the months of May to August 1992? Did he tell you where he was working?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Bosnia, of course I inquired what -- how my family was doing, what was going on. He told me that he had been mobilised, that he became a member of the reserve police force and that he was on duty in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you knew -- he told you that he was a reserve policeman and was mobilised in 1992. When you said Omarska, did he specifically say a specific place he was assigned to? Did he say that he was working in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No. These were telephone conversations. I inquired, and it was a regular kind of inquiry, I wanted to know the information, and my information was that he was a police officer at Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Curcic, you would have not discussed that. But then after you met him, did you ask him about the time that he spent in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: We never talked much about those activities. I don't know how to phrase it. He never specifically told me where -- I cannot ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You're trying to say that you didn't discuss the activities during that time, but he was a brother who was close to you. Did you ask him as to how he survived or what he -- how the times that he spent during these difficult times, especially during the month of May 1992? I'm sorry to ask you this question again, so you never discussed or he never told you as to what he did in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No, because even if I asked him this, he said that he preferred not to talk about it. Also because I was -- I had an illness when I was small, so he was trying to spare me, not to bring up certain subjects.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that he preferred not to speak about the time that he spent in the Omarska camp. Did you know that there was a camp in Omarska, a detention camp?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I knew that there was an investigation centre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you learn as to what, who -- what happened there, as to who was detained there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Specifically, no, because in that period I did not go to Omarska, and we spoke about that very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was there any good reason for you not to -- prefer not to speak about this time that Milojica spent in the Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I think I've already told you that he did not like to talk about this. In fact, he doesn't talk much at all. And because of my illness, he knew that I could get upset, and that was probably the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, I'm sorry, I have to ask you another question which is a little bit unclear to me. The summary which was provided to the Prosecution by the Defence says that you are an administration officer. Did you do any work in the administration?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: A summary which has been provided by your counsels to the Prosecution says that you are an administration officer.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Have you worked as an administration officer during your -- at any time?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Curcic, another small area I need to ask you about. By the way, the time that you spent in Lamovita and you said that you subsequently moved to Sivnica in Serbia, but at the time you spent with your brother, did you get to know any persons by the name of Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: When I was very small, when I passed by his parents' house I would see him and I would say hello. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was that in Omarska? He was in, if I may, the neighbourhood; is that correct? He was a person from the area?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know when he became -- after he became a police officer?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I did know him, but it never went beyond greeting each other, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he visit your brother when he was a police officer, the time that you knew?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know whether your brother knew Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: In the same way that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of Mladen Radic, another policeman from the Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: One Mr. Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Prcac, another police officer?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, but also just by greetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And this was prior to the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: That was up until 1984 when I left Lamovita and moved to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, I will take you to another area. Did you meet your brother in 1994?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, after 1992 -- that is, 1993, I saw him regularly, and "regularly" meant two to three times a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That was the time, if -- am I correct, the time that he was a policeman in Banja Luka, an active policeman?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know that he became an active policeman?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later, though, after he had been in the reserve police. I knew that he attended a course, but I don't know -- I didn't ask whether then that made him an active-duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you now know that he was an active policeman in 1994?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Whether it was in 1994 or when, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But do you know that he was an active policeman?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I know that he attended a course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, did you -- when did you get to know that he was indicted of war crimes?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: When I read it in the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have to ask you: Could you remember as to when, which year that was?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: If I said that the indictment was publicised in 1995, February, will you accept that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know when Mr. Milojica Kos was arrested?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: On 27 March -- 27 May 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In the year of 1998. So since -- from the time of, say, year 1995 and 1998, did you meet Milojica Kos during that period, your brother?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he has been indicted? Did you discuss about the indictment?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: That he did not consider himself guilty in any way, that this must be a mistake, and that he could not comprehend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he -- did you propose to him or did he want to surrender?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I never proposed that to him, nor did he ever tell me anything about his wish to surrender or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he lose his police status during this time, from the time that -- 1995 until the arrest in 1998?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Waidyaratne, the witness said that she only knew that he made a training course only, so that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Can I ask you whether you knew as to what your brother was doing from the year 1995 to the time of his arrest?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I know that he was in Banja Luka; that occasionally he worked in coffee bars and that that is how he made his livelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, I will ask you some little details about your brother. During the time that he worked in the reserve police in Omarska, did you know as to what his salary was, what remuneration he had?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he, at any time, provide you with financial assistance?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know as to whether he supported his family, his father and his stepmother, financially?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He provided assistance, of course. He bought whatever they needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, you said that your brother was a person who was involved in -- a happy man who was involved in sports but not involved in politics. If you know, do you know as to whether he had a tattoo engraved in his left arm?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes. He still has that tattoo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you remember what it is, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Two hearts and two letters, so far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you remember the two letters that were there? You would have seen it for a long time. If you remember.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: My apologies. I think it's a "J" and then an "N," something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: It's two letters, "J" and "N"; am I correct? Am I getting the translation?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, Milojica is not married.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he have a girlfriend that you knew?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were girls in his life. I may have known one or two but superficially only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: One was named Katarina; another one, Dragana.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Have you, by any chance -- have you had the chance of hearing the name Edna?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That concludes my cross-examination, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne. Ms. Nikolic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Curcic, what was the secondary school that you completed?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: The school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What title did you get after that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: It was an administrative worker.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were an administrative worker?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is your profession now?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I am a seamstress.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This is what you do?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you finished, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Judge Fouad Riad, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Mr. President. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mrs. Curcic, I just have two small questions. One, did you have anybody in your acquaintance back in Lamovita or Omarska who had been detained in the Omarska camp? Did you know anybody who had been there as a detainee?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: On your visits back to Lamovita after 1992, did anyone ever speak to you about your brother having been in the Omarska camp or anything he might have done while he was there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My last question is: You said that when the indictment came down, your brother said it was a mistake and he didn't know how that could have happened. At that time, did he say anything else about what his role was in the camp or what he actually did in the camp or anything that happened in the camp, when he was talking about it being a mistake, in his view, that he was indicted?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No. He only said, "This is impossible and this is a mistake."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's all?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Judge Wald. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mrs. Curcic, I have two questions, small questions, for you. I believe that you said that since January 1992 until January 1993, you contacted your brother by phone and that he told you at the time that he was on duty in Omarska. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he told me -- when I called him up and when I asked him, after the war had started and the mobilisation and all those things, I asked him where they were and if everybody was alive. When I talked to him, he told me that he had been mobilised as a reserve police officer in Omarska and that that's where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But what did you understand him to mean by telling you that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: At that moment, nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You weren't concerned? Didn't this prompt you to say, "Aren't you at the Omarska Police Station," or something like that?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: That was my understanding when he said that he was a member of the reserve police force in Omarska, because there was a single precinct there and that that's where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, was there a police station in Omarska at the time or not?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question. You said that after January 1993 you didn't speak too much about Omarska, you didn't say too much. When you mentioned Omarska, what does it imply to you? When you said here that you didn't discuss Omarska much, what exactly did you mean? I'm talking about January 1993.

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: The question was in reference to Omarska specifically, and we talked very little about the war and we really did not discuss that topic much at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but when you said that you didn't discuss Omarska much, which Omarska were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me explain, then. He was on duty in Omarska, that is what you heard on the phone, and you said you thought of Omarska and him being in the police reserve force, and you also said that there was a police station in Omarska. But in January 1993 you said that you discussed Omarska very slightly, but when you said Omarska, was it a village, a police station, a tourist resort? What was it?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: When I was in Omarska in January 1993 I attended the patron saint's celebration, and many people came through the house so that we did not have time to discuss any other matters. There were many friends, relatives, and the conversations were the usual daily ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry for interrupting you, Mrs. Curcic, but he said he preferred not to talk about "it." What was it that he didn't like to talk about, what subject?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: He is not a man of many words, so he doesn't discuss anything much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you said that he preferred not to explain things to you, so you don't know what it is that he didn't want to tell you about. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I never even asked him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Do you know whether he discussed this subject that he avoided discussing with you, did he discuss it with other persons?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So, Mrs. Curcic, that completes your testimony. Yes, I see I didn't ask the other Defence counsel whether they have any questions for this witness, so Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First off, Mr. Waidyaratne asked the witness whether she knew a person by the name of Mladen Radic. If this is some person that Mr. Waidyaratne is interested in, that is fine; but if this is in reference to the accused, that is not the accused's name. That is number one. The second thing I want to ask is whether the lady can distinguish between the, the Omarska Police Station and the Omarska Police Station Department. Does she make -- does she distinguish between these two?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My next question is, then, would she know whether there was a police station there or a department of the police station there?

utterances.speaker: NADA CURCIC
utterances.text: I really don't know the official title of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That completes my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, you have any other questions, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mrs. Curcic, this really is the end of your testimony. Thank you very much for coming here, and I shall ask the usher to accompany you out. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That exactly is what I wanted to suggest, that we should take a break before we call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We welcome your suggestion, Ms. Nikolic, so we're going to have a half-hour break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before we call our next witness, could D6/2 and D7/2 which have been marked for identification by the registry to be admitted into evidence, please. We should like to tender those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Nikolic. Nothing appears in the transcript as yet, though we heard what you said. I think it is beginning to work again. Yes. If I understood you correctly, Ms. Nikolic, you are asking for Exhibits D6/2 and D7/2 to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne? No. Therefore, the documents are admitted into evidence, Ms. Nikolic, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. The Defence now calls our next witness, Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Milan Babic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're now going to read the solemn declaration given to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for coming. First you will be answering questions put to you by the Defence counsel for Mr. Kos, that is, by Ms. Jelena Nikolic. You have the floor, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Babic, for identification purposes, will you tell us your particulars? Your name first.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: My name is Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The date of your birth?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: 23rd of October, 1971, in Bistrica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where is Bistrica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you complete your elementary education?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In Lamovita, and my secondary education in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What secondary school did you attend?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The secondary school of mechanical engineering.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was your occupation upon graduation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: A metal worker.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is your occupation today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I'm a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where are you employed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In the Special Police service of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What kind of jobs do you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I'm leader of a team for the use of official dogs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you collaborate with any United Nations agencies in your work?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: With which?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: IPTF and the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Before the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992, where were you living and working?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I was living in Bistrica, and I was working in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was your work post in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I was working in the Vrbas building construction enterprise as a woodworker.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Have you done your military service?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When and where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I served in Sibenik and Pula in 1990, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Milojica Kos?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you know Milojica Kos before the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Only by sight, when we would pass each other on the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: For how long did you know Mr. Kos in that way prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: From 1988 until 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what he was by occupation at the end of the 1980s?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He was a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I would see him in various coffee bars serving guests.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, let us go back briefly to 1992 and the outbreak of conflicts in the area. Where were you when the war started in Bosnia in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I was in the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: To the reserve police station in Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How were people drafted to the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In my case, I was mobilised because I had served in the navy. I didn't have a military assignment so they drafted me to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you undergo any police training?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have any experience as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In those days, were only young reservists mobilised to the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were older reservists also mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What does an older reservist actually mean?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: They were people who were reservists before the war, who had five or ten years of experience or more.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, please feel free to explain what you mean when talking about the experience of a reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It meant that before the war, he would have seminars, training exercises in handling weapons and familiarisation with police rules - these exercises would be held once or twice a year - whereas young reserve police officers had no training or lectures or seminars that they had attended before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether I have already asked you this, but in what month of 1992 were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: At the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you spend the period after mobilisation in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And where was it located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We were assigned to providing security of the transmitter at Mount Kozara and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was your actual duty at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We patrolled the settlements and provided security for the transmitter repeater.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Who was your immediate superior in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The station commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What station did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The police station at Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was it a permanent standing police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was it at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was a reserve police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were there any more experienced police officers with you young reservists?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How old was he?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Over 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was he a reservist or an active-duty policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He was a reservist with experience as a reserve police officer before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, how much experience did he have as a reserve policeman before the outbreak of conflicts?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: More than ten years' experience.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What were his tasks and duties, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: To coordinate the work of us reserve police officers; to assign us to work according to schedule. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you leave the reserve police station at Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of November -- no, on the first of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Will you explain to Your Honours how that came about and why?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: There was a vacancy in the police station for the admission of policemen to a special purpose unit in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you meet Milojica Kos again?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: On the way to Banja Luka on November the 1st.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You applied for that job that was announced as a vacancy. Did you ever complete a training course for a policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: From mid-January until the beginning of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did Milojica Kos ever complete a police training school; do you know? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, after me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Within the framework of the same institution or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, within the framework of the same institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what were the requirements for somebody to apply for that job and to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The requirements were completed secondary education, under 30 years of age, a certificate that there were no criminal charges or proceedings against one, and a medical certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What prompted you to apply for this job?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was also stated in the notification that we would be attending a course for active-duty policemen in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long did that course last?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was a six-month course.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Judges what it was like, what you were taught?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Three months of theoretical training and lectures, and three months of practical work in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have to sit for a final examination at the end of this training course for policemen?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long did that examination last?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, she didn't hear the answer to that question, how long did the exam last.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long was the final examination after you completed the course?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know who issued the certificate or diploma at the end of your course, and describe it if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska, that is, the secondary school for Internal Affairs in Banja Luka. The certificate is A4 in format, and it says, "Certificate On the Completion of the Police Course." It contains the particulars of the student, when the course began, and when it was completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher for his assistance to bring me Exhibit D5/2, and to show it to the witness, please. The Trial Chamber have copies, and my learned friends from the Prosecution as well. Could you please place the original on the ELMO and then he will be able to explain to Their Honours what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, you have looked at the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After the completion of your course, did you receive such a certificate, a similar certificate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How does this document in front of you differ from the one you received in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The difference is the name and the particulars of the student, and the duration also.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I don't need the document any more, you can collect it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you completed your course, Mr. Babic what was your title?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I acquired the title of an active-duty policeman, a beginner, an apprentice, an intern, an intern, a police intern.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you start working, and did you have to go through an internship or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Upon the completion of this course and when you acquired your diploma, did you get any rank?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While attending this course and lectures, were you familiarised for the first time with the laws in force at the time in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My colleague tells me that there's an error in the transcript, so allow me to repeat the question. After completing your course for a policeman and after you acquired your diploma, were you given a rank?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While attending that course, was that the first time you were familiarised with the rights and duties of policemen, the rules of service, the organisation of the police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to speak up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That's a very clear leading question by Ms. Nikolic at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Nikolic, please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll do that. That's easy enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, will you please tell us what subjects you studied at the course?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The Rules of Service, criminal law, material law, administrative law, physical education, traffic regulations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to the training you had then and the experience as a policeman now, can you tell us whether a reserve policeman has any position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does he have any command responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does a reserve policeman have any persons subordinated to him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can a reserve policeman be called in to do active duty?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No. Only under very exceptional and specific circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to Their Honours what those specific circumstances could be?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Should there be a shortage of personnel, a reserve policeman had to have higher education and could then get a job should there be a vacancy, but only in the administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, a new recruit, a reserve policeman, can he be asked to do active duty?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please be kind enough to clear up what you mean by "higher education," according to our educational system, to explain to everybody in the courtroom what we mean.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It had to be at least two years of post-secondary education at a university or at a higher educational institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the course of your stay in Banja Luka and while attending this course, did you have any contact with Milojica Kos?
