utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How often were the two of you together in 1992/1993?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: On a daily basis. We worked together and, for a time, we shared a room.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you socialise in your free time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Babic, but please move up to the microphone so that the interpreters can hear you better. Thank you. Did you socialise with him in your free time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you met in 1992, as you described, on your way to Banja Luka, did you know what he was at the time and whether he worked in the police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I knew that he was a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: All of us who underwent that course, who had applied for the job, were reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As a man who spent a period of his life socialising with Milojica Kos, can you tell us what kind of man he is? How would you describe him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He is very withdrawn, but he is also sociable at the same time. He always liked people. He liked everybody. He socialised with everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he ever expressed any political views?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were police officers able to be members of political parties?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was usually the topic of your discussions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We talked about the good old times before the war, what we did before and what was the situation now. We talked about private problems, about friends, families, about problems we had with feeding ourselves, providing for our family, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you were together, when you talked to each other, did Milojica Kos ever express his opinion about other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did he ever show signs of any ethnic hatred or lack of tolerance?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Babic. Thank you, Your Honours. I have completed the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much. Any other Defence counsel who wish to examine the witness? No? Thank you. Mr. Waidyaratne, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Babic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, could you tell me your father's name, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Momir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And your mother?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Milena.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that you were born in Bistrica, am I correct, in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How far is it from Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Between 7 and 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Milojica Kos during your childhood?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Am I correct if I say that you saw him sometimes when he was in Omarska, but other than that, you had no relationship with him until you got to know him in 1992, when you went to Banja Luka? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, do you have any nicknames? Are you called by the name of Babi?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you have any other names?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, do you know that Mr. Kos has a house in Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he speak about that house when he was put up with you in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He mentioned a few times that he had started building a house before the war but that he stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the past three years; that is, three years ago I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, today to come to the Tribunal, you left Banja Luka; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What is the address where you live, where do you live in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Omladinska Street, house number 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Is it correct if I say that it is a house of Mr. Kos?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Kos has a house in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He was only using a state-owned apartment who was given to the Ministry of the Internal Affairs by municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So he had a flat or an annex or house in Banja Luka; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He had the right to use the flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you live with Mr. Kos in the same house?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Babic the time that you spent with Mr. Kos, you said that he used to discuss, other than politics, about other matters. Did he mention anything about the time that he spent at the Omarska camp in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: He never spoke with you or discussed with you about the times that he spent as a reserve policeman in the Omarska camp? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that he was a reserve police officer, but not where he worked and what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Babic, now in 1992 you said that you were attached to -- you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Attached to the Lamovita police station, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. The reserve station of -- the reserve police station in Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, this reserve police station in Lamovita, what are the areas that this police station covered?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It covered the settlements in the area of Gornja Lamovita, the village of Bistrica. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did it cover the area of Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did it cover the village of Babici?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. That village is part of Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So what are the villages, if I may ask you much clearly, that was covered by the Lamovita police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Babici, Perici, Stojakovici, and the village of Bistrica, which included Gornja Bistrica and Donja Bistrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did it cover the village of Verici?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, not Verici. They didn't fall under the area of the Lamovita police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that you were assigned to during 1992, to protect the transmitter in Mount Kozarac. Did Lamovita cover that area, too, or was it due to the special assignment that was given to your unit that you had to go to Mount Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No. It was part of the area which was covered by the Lamovita police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So that means Mount Kozarac, a certain part of mount Kozarac also comes under Lamovita?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who are the others who were in the special unit with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I can repeat it. Can you remember the other personnel who was with you in the special unit that was doing duty with you during 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the transmitter on the Kozara mount?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll start there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was not the special unit which was involved there, but I do remember some of the people. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you tell us the names of those people that you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Radenko Kukic, Mirko Milicevic, Slobodan Milicevic, Ljubo Paspalj, Jovan Paspalj, Milenko Macanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was there a person by the name of Dragan Babic with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Not in the area which we covered, that is, the transmitter and the surrounding villages, that is, the area which stretches on towards Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Babic, what, exactly did you do when you say that you gave security to the transmitter? Why was it necessary during that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We had an order to that effect from the police station; that is, to provide security for the transmitter and to patrol the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The commander of the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Grahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Is it Ljuban?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he specifically say as to what you all should do when you go on this assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Just provide security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What uniforms did you wear, did you wear?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. A police uniform, because uniforms changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Right. Did you change your uniform subsequently?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "subsequently"?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: As a police officer. From the answer that you gave me earlier, you seem to have changed the uniforms. Did you change your uniform subsequently when you were serving in the Lamovita police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No. I'm really sorry, but I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you by any chance wear an olive-grey uniform during the time that you were providing security duty at Mount Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What is this uniform? Could you tell the Chamber as to what this uniform is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was a multicoloured, that is, camouflage, uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And that was other than the police uniform that you generally wore as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Because we didn't have adequate uniforms, we wore insignia on our shoulders, and the insignia were those of a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And a camouflage/multicoloured uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, were you, at any time, attached to the 16th Krajina Brigade of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, the time that you went on -- we will cover this area quickly. The time that you went on this guard duty, you were provided with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What kind of weapon did you carry?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: M-48 rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That's an automatic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, semiautomatic. No, no, not even semiautomatic, but it was a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During the time that you served the military, in the navy, you had training with -- weapon training.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: As a member of the navy, I had very little training of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But you know how to shoot and how to use a gun.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Babic, did you, during the time that you served in Lamovita, at any time, cover the area of Tukovi, in the month of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During this time, did you also -- were you assigned to or were you mobilised in the area of Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, the time that you spent in -- provided security to Mount Kozarac, did you see the surrounding areas, as to what happened in those areas?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How about the houses, the people who lived there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We just heard sounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, are you trying to tell the Chamber that during this time that you served in the Lamovita Police Station, that you did not know or you didn't see as to what happened in the areas of Kozarac, Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, no, we didn't see it. We didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did you hear as to what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that you heard certain things but you didn't see. What did you hear? Could you tell the Chamber as to what you heard?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We heard noise which came from shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know as to what happened after the shelling?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: At that time, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Later on, did you get to know as to what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did you hear? What did you get to know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: We learned about it through various stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: That there had been shelling in the area of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you observe any houses of non-Muslims damaged -- Muslims, houses of Muslims, non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I saw that six or seven months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During the time that -- in the month of July, June and July, you didn't see this damage?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You are a policeman who visited -- went out of the police station, who was mobilised. You're telling the Chamber that you didn't see this damage which had been done; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I did leave the police station, but I was focused on Banja Luka. I didn't go in the direction of Prijedor, because I planned to live in Banja Luka, I had family there, and I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I'm unable to accept your explanation. I don't know whether I do understand you properly. But the time -- during the time that you served as a reserve policeman in Lamovita and were assigned to do duty, patrolling, say, providing security to Mount Kozarac, did you see any damage caused to the houses of the Muslims or non-Serbs, and non-Serbs being removed from that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: One couldn't see anything from the transmitter because of the woods. The area is a distant one, and this is where I worked, this is where I was posted. Whereas other people from the police station were in charge of other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I let my learned colleague ask a number of questions on this particular topic and the witness has provided answers to all of those questions. But the last question is a confusing one and a leading one; moreover, I think that the witness has already answered the question. However, there is something confusing in the record concerning various locations and localities. I will bring it up during my re-examination. I believe that that is actually the cause of this confusion. Let me say what the problem is. There has been a confusion between Kozara and Kozarac in the record. The way things stand now, this seems to be one and the same location, but there is a difference between the Kozara Mountain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Nikolic, you will have an opportunity to clarify that during your re-examination. We have noticed that. Mr. Waidyaratne, are you aware of the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what is the result of that awareness of yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it has expired. You had 25 minutes, so you have no more time left, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I would beg your indulgence for a few more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three, I will give you three minutes to finish your cross-examination, Mr. Waidyaratne. It is a rule that we established a long time ago. You have to be able to control the time that has been allotted to you. If you have important questions, proceed with your important questions. If I were you, if I were aware of this time restriction, I would begin with asking important questions, and then later on continue with other questions. Three minutes to finish your cross-examination, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, did Mr. Kos tell you about the time -- you said that he didn't discuss the time that he spent in Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was a camp which detained non-Serbs in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you ever go to that camp?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know as to who were detained there and as to why those people were detained there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kos tell you, during the time that he spent with you in Banja Luka, as to why those people were detained there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kos tell you as to what exactly he did in the Omarska camp as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a leading question, the one that we had from the beginning. In response to the first question put by my learned colleague, the witness said no, that is, that he was not in the camp. I believe that the witness has already clearly answered the question, and now the question is being asked for the second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nikolic, you're right. Mr. Waidyaratne, you started with the question, "Did Mr. Kos talk to you about Omarska?" and he said, "No," and then you continue with matters that would have been the topic of the conversation. Do you realise what you've done?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I do. This question was because we discussed certain matters after that, and I refreshed his mind. I thought he may be able to recollect certain new things. That's why I posed that question. Thank you, Your Honour, I will not repeat myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kos ever say that he wanted to leave the police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he enjoy being a policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But he never regretted being a policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he seem to be satisfied with the conversations that you had with him, that the time he spent as a policeman? Was he satisfied that he was a policeman and the functions that he performed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He wasn't satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said earlier something contradictory. Could you explain yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't know what period of time you have in mind, whether the time that he spent as a reserve police officer or an active-duty police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: As a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No. He wasn't satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Because of the living conditions at that time and because of professional conditions; that is, relating to the work in general, he wasn't satisfied. He could not be satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was it, was it the --

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He was not familiar enough with the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The salary?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the biggest problem. There was no salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: My last question to Mr. Babic, Your Honour. I'll conclude after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Kos satisfied being a policeman than being a waiter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Being a waiter. I don't quite understand. Did you mean before that or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did he enjoy? Was it as a policeman or as a waiter? What did he prefer to do, did he say anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: As a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, do you know when Mr. Kos left his position as an active policeman, or whether he did leave at all until his arrest?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, he stopped working after the indictment was issued, after the indictment was publicly announced.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know when?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just to let you know that you didn't take three minutes but six minutes, but thank you anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, would you please tell the Judges what Mr. Kos did after he was released from the police duty?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I do know he worked as a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where did he work as a waiter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And just to clarify a confusion, will you please tell us this: Just if you -- you said that he worked as a waiter in Banja Luka, when was this, if you recall, what year this was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: After 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Is this the job that he worked at until he was arrested, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you tell us where your unit was located when you were a member of the reserve in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: You mean where I worked or where the station was? 25 Q. Where your deployment was. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: At the transmitter, in the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Will you please tell us, what is Kozara?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: That is a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know, does the name Kozarac mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What is Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Kozarac is a village, the foothills of Mount Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the place where you were deployed on Mount Kozara, how far is that from the village of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: About 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Nikolic. Judge Fouad Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Babic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just have a supplementary question to clarify more what you said. If I understood rightly, you shared the room with Mr. Kos in 1992 and even after that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: From 1 November 1992 until the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And were you socialising before that, too, or after that? You knew each other a long time before?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You did not socialise before November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And when you started living together, he never, as you said to Mr. Waidyaratne, he never discussed with you the time he spent in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you feel that was some kind of taboo, something he would never speak of?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No, that was not a taboo subject. He was just a withdrawn person. He kept to himself. He was not known for talking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, one question. At any point in any of the training courses or lectures that you received, either as a reserve or when you were getting ready to be an active policeman, did you receive training in the international humanitarian law that applies to anybody who performs functions in wartime, performs police or like functions in wartime? Did you receive any kind of training about the Geneva Conventions and that sort of thing, and if so, at what point in your career?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard while I was attending the courses in Banja Luka in 1993, in January 1993. Let's say mid-January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You were given -- you say you heard, you were given some kind of lectures or some kind of written material to familiarise yourself with what that international humanitarian law was at that time, in January 1993? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: During the course, we had one class a week which dealt with the international law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Now, just to follow that up, before that when you were mobilised way back in -- I don't know whether it was April or May, but whenever you were mobilised as a reserve policeman before you went to the Banja Luka training course, when you took up your duties as a reserve policeman at the Lamovita police station, did you get any kind of training like that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Judge Wald. Mr. Babic, did a time come when you learnt that Mr. Kos had worked in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I learned about it when the indictment was made public, that he was alleged to be a war crimes suspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I understood you well, you have already touched upon the matter slightly, that is, that you shared the same room with Mr. Kos from the 1st of November until the end of 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that would be almost a year and a half, a year and one month, a year and one month?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you lived in the same room with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, we shared it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also said that you worked together. For how long did you work together?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: About a year and a half to two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. You also said that the subject of conversation, of your conversations, were basically the war and concerns linked to the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No. The subject was not the war but, rather, the life before the war, mostly the problems relating to the families, then sport topics, sometimes about going out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say that you spoke about the conditions prior to the war, was there any particular area that you compared, or was it simply nostalgia for good old times?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was regretting the passage of the good old days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not trying to lead you into giving us an answer. You were comparing the situation before the war and now the situation during the war or after the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Today, Mr. Babic, you know that Mr. Kos worked in the Omarska camp, that he was a reserve policeman in the Omarska camp. You shared the same room with him; you worked together for more than a year. What is your impression today as to why Mr. Kos did not mention these things at the time? I'm not asking you for the reasons going through Mr. Kos' mind and heart, I'm asking you what you think, how you would interpret this, what your feelings about it are.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I don't know. As I said, Milojica was a fairly withdrawn person. He did not like to talk about this, nor did I insist on it. I would not like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What things? You're not insisting now or at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: At that time, I did not express interest in where he was, what he did. That was his personal matter. We discussed all other topics outside of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Babic, but you had just attended a course to become a policeman, and that activity had something to do with the activity for which you were trained. To be a reserve policeman in the Omarska camp, does it have anything to do with the training that you underwent together?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: My apologies, but could you please repeat the question? I did not fully follow it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be glad to. My question is the following: To be a reserve policeman in the Omarska camp, and the experience that Kos had when he was there, did it have anything in common with the training that you went through together? Is it related?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It probably is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Babic, you have just completed your testimony here. Thank you very much for coming, and I shall ask the usher to accompany you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is time to have the lunch break now. I think that you have already been informed that we will have a Status Conference today at 4.00, just so that you know. I have already given some indication to that effect. We shall now have a 50-minute break. Fifty minutes. I'm looking at the clock. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.50 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Yes, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence calls the witness Zeljko Srdic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Zeljko Srdic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read the solemn declaration given to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Make yourself as comfortable as possible, and you will first be answering questions put to you by Mr. Nikolic standing to your left. That's better, but you know the questions by heart, Mr. Nikolic, so there's no problem for you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. You're right about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Srdic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: For the record, will you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: My name is Zeljko Srdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell us your exact date of birth?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: 10 December 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Crni Vrh in Glamoc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you have any education?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you complete your elementary school?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I completed it in the local commune of Rore.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After the primary schooling, did you continue with your education?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where did you enroll next?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: After the elementary school I enrolled in the forestry secondary school in Glamoc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where was this school exactly?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: It was in the town of Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you graduate from that school?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I graduated in 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After graduating from the school, what did you become?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I worked in the jobs for which I became qualified through this training.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Which was what exactly?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: That was the job of the forestry technician in the company where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After finishing your secondary school, did you immediately find a job?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I started working a few months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, did you do your military service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did do my military service in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us in what year and where you went to serve your military service?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I served in the years 1989 to 1990, in the city of Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After having completed your military service, did you continue to work in the job for which you had been trained?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I continued to work in the same job.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, are you a family man?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Freshly married.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, before the war broke out in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, where were you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I was in my home municipality of Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After having served out your military duties, were you ever mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: After I completed this military service, I just continued working in my regular job and I was a member of the reserve, like everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, when exactly were you mobilised in the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: That was on 20 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where were you mobilised in the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: That was in Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, would you please explain, where exactly is Glamoc located in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Glamoc is about 130 kilometres southwest of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From the moment of your mobilisation, did you ever come to Banja Luka or Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about events in that area in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: You mean Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Banja Luka and Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You said that you were mobilised as a member of the reserve police force. Will you now please tell us what your duties were, and what did you do as a reserve police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised in the reserve police force. I worked as an assistant helping the active-duty police officers in discharging their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you work on your own?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No. We always worked in groups of three.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Who were the members of those groups of three?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: A group always consisted of one active-duty police officer and two reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, at the time when you were mobilised, who was your direct superior officer?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: My direct superior officer, at the time of my mobilisation, was the commander of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In Glamoc?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the commander of the Glamoc Police Station was an active-duty police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, with an advanced degree in police training.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were mobilised as a reserve police officer, at the time of the mobilisation, did you get any kind of training for the job and duties that you were to carry out as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, I did not get any type of training.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: During the period that you spent working as a reserve police officer, that is, in that period of time, did you receive any kind of training?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Through the work, on the ground, with the assistance of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. active-duty police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The place where you worked as a reserve police officer, were you able to do something on your own, independently, or to order someone to do something?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From the moment when you were mobilised, how long did you work as a reserve police officer in Glamoc?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I worked until November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I went to Banja Luka for a training course for police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So you came to Banja Luka in order to attend --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: To attend a training course for an active-duty police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How did you find out about these training courses?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: It was in the newspapers, and also I saw the advertisement on the bulletin board in the police station in Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were there any conditions, were there any requirements for a person to be admitted to such a course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were requirements and they consisted of a certain education, the check of the criminal record, and certain health conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From what you know, was anybody admitted to this course who -- among those who did not fulfil those requirements?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: From what I know, no one who did not fulfil these requirements could be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The training course that you were admitted to, when did it start?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: My class started in mid-January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long did this course take?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: It took six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you recall today, how was this course designed, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: It was three months of theoretical courses, and then three months of practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And this practical portion of the course, where did you carry that out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: That was in the special purpose brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was that in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While you were attending this training course, did you for the first time learn about legal provisions involved?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in now is whether this practical part of the course was in some ways implementation of the theory that you had covered in the previous part of the course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, after finishing -- after having finished the course, did you have to pass a final exam?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how long this final exam took, how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. It took two to three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After you completed the course, did you receive a certificate?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received a certificate of completion of the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And what did you become after you completed this course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: After I completed this course, I became a junior police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Upon completion of the course, did you get any rank?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What happened to you when you completed the course and received your certificate?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: When I completed the course and received my certificate, I started working as a police officer in the special purpose brigade in the OBL department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The station to which you were assigned, did you immediately start working as an active-duty policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Not straight away because a certain period is required of so-called internship, which lasts six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you explain more closely what that means in practice?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: This internship in practice means that the young policeman has to become acquainted with the methods of work applied in the police, in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, are you aware whether it is possible for a reserve policeman to become an active-duty policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that possibility in the way in which I was transferred from a reserve policeman to an active-duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So you went to a course and got a certificate?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, and thus I became an active-duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of anybody without attending such a course becoming an active-duty policeman after being a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: To round off this topic I wish to ask you, what were your motives in applying for this course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: When the announcement appeared on the bulletin board in the station I was working in, I applied for admission. The motives were of a material nature, resolving the problem of housing for myself, mainly questions of livelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are you still working in the police?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the brigade for anti-terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So you will agree with me that your work in the police was uninterrupted ever since you graduated from the course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, uninterrupted to the present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after the date when the course was signed, did the IPTF vet the police personnel in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and they did so on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you checked once or several times, if there were several checks?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was cleared after all three checks, and I received an appropriate certificate from the IPTF.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If you hadn't received that certificate from the IPTF, could you have continued working in the police?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, I could not have continued working in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, do you know a person by the name of Milojica Kos?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Mr. Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you meet Mr. Kos?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I met Mr. Milojica Kos in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what Milojica Kos did when you met?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: When we met, he was a reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did the two of you meet?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: We met in Banja Luka at the Internacional Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You said he was a reserve policeman at the time you met. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: He told me that when we were introduced to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the original occupation of Mr. Kos is?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: The basic occupation of Mr. Kos was in the catering business, and he was a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I learnt it from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you socialised?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How often would you see one another?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Well, occasionally, two or three times a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you in the same generation at the training course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, we were not in the same generation. I was the class prior to his.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for us Milojica Kos's personality as you saw him?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. As far as I know him, he was a friendly man, he was popular in company. Briefly, a person that everyone would like to have as a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us a little about his temperament?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Temperament? He's quiet, withdrawn, and always smiling.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember in -- at the time when you were friendly and when you socialised, what were the topics you discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Well, sports, that was a way when we -- we also got together through sports. We would play basketball for recreational purposes. We would play billiards. We would go out on dates with girls. We would engage in other games.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, did Milojica Kos graduate from the same course that you graduated from?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After the completion of that course, what did Mr. Milojica Kos become?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: He also became a junior policeman like myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Srdic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Nikolic. Any other counsel who would like to examine this witness? I see negative signs. Mr. Saxon, you have the floor to cross-examine this witness, and you have more or less 20 minutes for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, I hope I am pronouncing your name correctly.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You described how you were mobilised into the reserve police force in September of 1991, and you remained as a reserve policeman until November of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct, quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During that period of time, you were serving in Glamoc?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: In the police station in Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During that time period when you were serving as a reserve policeman, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was armed with a long-barrelled rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that rifle loaded?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: The rifle I was issued was loaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you trained at some point how to use it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I learned that while doing my military service in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During that time period, between September 1991 and November 1992, in your capacity as a reserve police officer, did you ever arrest anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I personally have never arrested anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During that time period, did you help any of your colleagues arrest anybody?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I didn't have occasion to do that because I worked in a group that was in charge of traffic control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, excuse me. Mr. Srdic, to put you at ease - I would like you to feel at ease - I wish to tell you that the microphone to the right is on. Both microphones are on, so please feel completely comfortable and speak normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the town of Glamoc, was there a gaol?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no prison in Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was there any place in Glamoc, if someone had to be arrested for any kind of crime, where they would be detained, even if just temporarily?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Personally, I don't know, but I think there was such a room in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you ever observe persons held in that room in the police station, even just briefly?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I did not because I was outside on the main road from Glamoc to Drvar, so that I went to the police station only on a couple of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you were doing traffic control, does that mean you and your colleagues occasionally would have to stop vehicles for different reasons?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did stop vehicles. In fact, we stopped all the vehicles, more or less, that passed through the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you or any of your colleagues ever beat any of the drivers or occupants of those vehicles that you stopped at your checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No. Our control was mainly limited to routine control of luggage and goods that were being transported through that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you or any of your colleagues ever sexually abuse any of the drivers or the occupants of the vehicles that you stopped at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you or any of your colleagues ever take away the valuables, wallets and jewellery, et cetera, from any of the drivers or the occupants of the vehicles that you stopped at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, I do not know of any form of corruption or any such acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In fact, between September 1991 and November 1992, did you ever see any of your colleagues in the police force or in the reserve police force mistreat citizens?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned the six-month course that you attended in Banja Luka, and at one point during your direct testimony, you talked about the legal provisions that were studied during that course. I'm wondering whether, during that course, you or your classmates or your instructors ever discussed examples of poor or improper police conduct.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No, never. The job of the policeman is to protect citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During that course, did you or any of your classmates or your instructors ever discuss activities at the Omarska camp or the Omarska investigations centre during the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: While we were attending the course, I was not familiar with any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That course began in January of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims in your course?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: At the time in Banja Luka, I don't think there was a single Muslim who was attending the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: This was a course organised for the Banja Luka region and students were exclusively of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you of Serb ethnicity yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, after the creation of the Republika Srpska in 1992, did you ever sign a declaration or an oath proclaiming that you would uphold the constitution and the laws of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Upon graduating from the course, I signed such an oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask for the usher's help, please. If we could place by the witness, on the ELMO, a copy of Prosecutor's Exhibit 3/210. I don't know if this is an exhibit that's been given to the Judges or not at this time. If not, it can be now. I think the members of the Defence need a copy of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Srdic, do you have a copy of the Serbo-Croatian text in front of you so that you can read it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can see, this is a document entitled "Solemn Declaration," it's dated 5th of May, 1992, and there is a signature on the bottom Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. right-hand side that purports to be the signature of Milojica Kos. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question for you is, the declaration or the oath that you signed when you completed your course, did it resemble this solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did not sign any such declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'm a little bit confused because I thought your response a moment ago was that you had. I'm looking at the transcript, page 79, line 19, where I asked you if you ever signed a declaration, and your response was, "Upon graduating from the course, I signed such an oath." Do you recall saying that to me?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I remember saying that, but I didn't sign any statement. Simply by getting the certificate, it meant that I was committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me read this to you. It says: "I, Milojica Kos, declare that I will perform the duty of an authorised official in a conscientious and responsible manner, that I will uphold the constitution and the laws and that I will protect the established order of the Republic, its laws, its liberties, and its security with all my strength; and that I will perform these and other duties and tasks of an authorised official even when performance of these duties and tasks may endanger my life." When you say that you got your certificate it meant you were committed, are you saying that when you received your certificate as a police officer, you were making the same commitment as is expressed in this declaration?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a solemn declaration orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did every graduate of your course, your police course, your police training course in Banja Luka, have to give this solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes. We all had to give that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that exhibit could be removed now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that upon your graduation, Mr. Srdic, you began to work in something called the Special Purpose Brigade. What was the purpose of the Special Purpose Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: A brigade for special purposes in the OBL department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that that was the name of the brigade, I guess in the context of police work, why did that brigade have the name "special purpose"? What were the special purpose or special activities that your brigade was expected to fulfil?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: The special tasks assigned to our brigade meant going to the front lines when necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know if Milojica Kos was ever a member of the Special Purposes Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the Special Purpose Brigade in the OBL department, together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you serve with Mr. Kos at the front line?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did go to the front line together on a couple of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you were together with Mr. Kos at the front line, did you and Mr. Kos face combat together?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: There were occasions of combat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have to volunteer to be a member of the Special Purpose Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: No. We applied once such an announcement was made public inviting applicants.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have to apply for acceptance into the Special Purposes Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: We were assigned to the Special Purposes Brigade in the OBL department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kos also apply to be a part of the Special Purpose Brigade, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Once we graduated from the course, we were assigned to this Special Purposes Brigade of the OBL department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you explain, what is the OBL department? Is OBL a place? Can you explain to the Judges what OBL is or where it is?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: The OBL department was a department for the security of important facilities in town and personalities, like the radio television of Republika Srpska, the central bank, and the other vital facilities in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that the IPTF vetted the policemen in Banja Luka three different times. Did you tell the representatives of the IPTF honestly and completely what you did during the war, during those vetting processes?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Isn't it true that when the IPTF performs those vetting procedures, they only ask serving police officers whether they have ever been arrested in the past or ever been convicted of a crime in the past? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Not a single policeman who had not -- whose criminal records had not been checked to make sure that they had none could work as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if you had never been arrested, had never been convicted of a crime, you could pass the IPTF vetting procedure; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I passed through the vetting procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I have the Court's indulgence for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Twenty minutes on the dot. So, Mr. Nikolic, is giving me a sign to tell me he has no additional questions. Judge Fouad Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: During the time when you were a reserve policeman, before you took the course to become an active policeman, and while you had been mobilised as a reserve policeman, suppose the assignment you had been given, you didn't like at all, you were unhappy with, you were very -- you didn't like the work and you really felt very dissatisfied, would you be able, as a mobilised reserve officer, to go to somebody and say, "I want a change of assignment," or were you absolutely required to stick to the assignment you had even if you were very unhappy about it? Was there any recourse if you really didn't like what you were doing? You were willing to be mobilised but you just wanted to do something else.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: I could not change my assignment. I could not carry it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I know you couldn't change it without permission of your superior, but could you go to the superior and ask for a change? Did that ever happen to anyone, in your experience? For various reasons - they didn't like where they had been assigned or they had family reasons or something - could they request a change?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: As far as the change of assignment is concerned, I could not influence that. The only thing I could do is to refuse to obey it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You couldn't just go to your commander and say, "Here are the reasons why. This is just a wrong assignment for me. I'll do something else, I'll do anything else you want me to do, but this is a bad place for me to be"? You couldn't do that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could make a suggestion; however, I could not influence a change in assignment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand that. In your experience, did that ever happen? Did anybody who was mobilised as a reserve policeman and assigned to one job ever request and have the request granted to be changed to a different assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, no, there were no such cases in my experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Judge Wald. Mr. Srdic, if I understood you well, but I would like to hear your answer, the course you attended ended in mid-July.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: The course I attended ended about mid-June or mid-July, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was six months, and if it started in mid-January, we can work it out. But there's another point, Mr. Srdic. At the end of this course, was there a ceremony or something to observe the completion of the course, to distribute diplomas, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a ceremony when these certificates/diplomas were given out, and then it was followed by some kind of a little party where refreshments were served.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How, where, and when did you give that solemn declaration that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: The solemn declaration was given at the premises where we had actually attended the courses, in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there were various places. You completed the course, the three months of practical training, and then you gave that solemn declaration in that room there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Srdic. I see that Judge Fouad Riad does have a question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. [In English] Mr. Srdic, in your answer to my colleague, Judge Wald, when she asked you if you could ask for a change of assignment, you said you could only refuse to obey an assignment. Was that allowed, to refuse an assignment, to refuse to obey, and what would be the result?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: It was not permitted. It was actually sanctioned by the superiors, and if I was not in a position to carry it out -- that is, unless I was not in a position to carry it out, that I had reasons for refusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And what would be the reasons? What reasons were you allowed to use?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: A reason for refusal would perhaps be, in my case, some lack of proper training to carry out an assignment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What about if the assignment was not a regular one or was a violation of any rules that you knew of, like assigning you to do a job, something which is not allowed, where your superior gave you an assignment which you know is not legally allowed?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: In my case, I just assisted the work of the active-duty police officers at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We're not speaking of your case because you were speaking in general. You said you could only refuse to obey an assignment. So does this refusal include also wrong assignments or assignments which you know are not legally correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SRDIC
utterances.text: My position is that I can refuse to carry out an assignment if this assignment is not legal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Srdic, you have just completed your testimony here. Thank you very much. The usher will now see you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, the Prosecutor would move for the admission of Prosecution Exhibit 3/210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there any objection, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, we object, Your Honour. There's no indicia of authenticity, of provenance, whether or not this person -- who this person is, no basis -- there's no indicia of it having any probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, your response to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Obviously this document is hearsay evidence; however, the standard for admission of hearsay before this Tribunal comes to us from the jurisprudence of Tadic where the party asking to admit the evidence must show relevance, probative value, and only an indicia of authenticity. I think the relevance and probative value are clear from the face of the document.
