This is a declaration signed by the accused, Mr. Kos, declaring that he will uphold the constitution and the laws of the Republika Srpska. It's signed in Prijedor, the 5 of May, 1992. The last witness indicated that all graduates of the training course in Banja Luka had to take such a declaration, a similar declaration, but here we have Mr. Kos making this declaration more than a year earlier. In terms of indicia of authenticity, we do have provenance. We know where this document was issued. It was issued by the Public Security Station from Prijedor. So in the Prosecutor's submission, this is clearly an admissible document. If there are issues as to probative value or authenticity, then the Trial Chamber at the end of the day may study those issues and determine what weight, if any, to give this document. Certainly it is admissible at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, I think the question that Mr. O'Sullivan has raised, if I understood him properly, is the question of the signature after all, the signature by the person involved. What the Defence is contesting is the authenticity, but specifically of the signature, but I'll give the floor to Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'll respond in three ways, Your Honour. First, there's no proof in the record that this document comes from Banja Luka; second, there's no proof that Milojica Kos was ever in Prijedor in early May 1992, no proof on the record of that; and clearly there's no proof whether we're talking about the same Milojica Kos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we're going on to another question. We've already addressed that matter. To produce a document, in my view, needs -- the first question that needs to be resolved is the question of authenticity. Do you have any response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and my submission is that the authenticity or indicia of authenticity of this document is visible from the face of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But how can you see that, Mr. Saxon? I personally don't see that. This document, I'm sorry, but it could have been prepared anywhere. How can you say that one can see the authenticity? Where did you get this document? Who gave you this document? I'm sorry for insisting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will respond in two ways. First of all, as Judge Wald suggested to us last week, we can and we will certainly submit a declaration of the investigator who seized these documents in Prijedor if that will assist the Court in determining sufficient authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: How about the original of this? Have you got the original in the Prosecutor's files? I mean, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The original should be in the Evidence Unit, in the Evidence Unit's vault or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: In the registry -- or I don't know where. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Whoever manages the Evidence Unit, it has always been the practice that the Evidence Unit holds on to the original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: The Evidence Unit of what, of the OTP or of the registry? I'm sorry, I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's my understanding that prior to evidence being admitted into Court, the evidence is maintained by the Evidence Unit of the Office of the Prosecutor, and then after that it would go to the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, don't you think that if a -- let me ask your opinion. If a document is challenged on authenticity, does the Prosecutor have an obligation to produce in Court the original and say, "Are you saying this isn't Mr. Kos's signature?" Or you think that they don't have that right, that it's enough just to have the Xerox of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honour. If a document is challenged, then the Prosecution -- if a Xerox copy of an original is presented in court and that is challenged, it is certainly fair to ask the Prosecution to show the original in Court, and that is something that we can do. If you would like, Your Honours, we can certainly hold this decision -- or you might hold this decision in abeyance for a day or two until we get a declaration from our investigator regarding this specific document, and we will do that. And we will also bring the original to court as soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You will present the report of the investigator, so we'll wait. We cannot decide now whether we're going to admit the document or not. But following on to what Judge Wald has just said, there was recently an amendment to the rules of the Tribunal which makes it obligatory that originals of documents that are photocopied, that the originals have to remain with the registry. In other words, the originals of the documents that you produce here in the courtroom have to be deposited with the registry. I cannot tell you by heart what exactly the amendment is, but it is to that effect. Therefore, since this latest amendment, you can no longer say that the original is any particular unit of the Prosecution; it has to be in the hands of the registry. With those remarks, you, Mr. Saxon, and the Prosecution as a whole can see what is happening, what will happen to this document afterwards. But anyway, we can't make a decision now. We will wait for the statement of the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, I don't suppose that we can begin with another witness now?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you're quite right. I misjudged the time. We completed earlier than we had planned, so I would like to resume with witness statements tomorrow at 9.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Nikolic, we're glad that you have finished earlier. We don't need to prolong things artificially, to use the time, so congratulations for doing your work so quickly. That is what should be said. So we will continue tomorrow according to the schedule, but we'll be back here at 4.00 for the Status Conference.
